<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as beef

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-beef" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-beef-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of beef, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" id="hmi-occurrence-beef-methods" data-shared-occurrence-methods><summary>Shared dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:beef-e224688ae715:312452ea6168"><summary>HMI beef Pb reference · Beef, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:beef-e224688ae715:312452ea6168"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI beef Pb reference · Beef, as sold. Beef, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤5</td><td>≤10</td><td>8.2–10 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤5</td><td>≤10</td><td>8.2–10 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>88 reference units; 5 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>78</td><td>20%</td></tr><tr><td>Henríquez-Hernández et al. 2023</td><td>2</td><td>20%</td></tr><tr><td>Mohamed et al. 2023</td><td>4</td><td>20%</td></tr><tr><td>Stojanović et al. 2021</td><td>3</td><td>20%</td></tr><tr><td>Szkoda et al. 2013</td><td>1</td><td>20%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for beef, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>5 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/henriquez-hernandez2023-baby-purees-spain-elements" class="internal" data-slug="sources/henriquez-hernandez2023-baby-purees-spain-elements" data-no-cite-meta>Henríquez-Hernández et al. 2023</a></li><li><a href="../sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt" class="internal" data-slug="sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt" data-no-cite-meta>Mohamed et al. 2023</a></li><li><a href="../sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Stojanović et al. 2021</a></li><li><a href="../sources/szkoda2013-poland-animal-tissues-milk-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/szkoda2013-poland-animal-tissues-milk-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Szkoda et al. 2013</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:beef-e224688ae715:312452ea6168</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:beef-6058d0f97b45:82d2285209fc"><summary>HMI beef Pb reference · Beef, as sold, basis not stated</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:beef-6058d0f97b45:82d2285209fc"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI beef Pb reference · Beef, as sold, basis not stated. Beef, as sold; Basis not stated by the source, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>2.3</td><td>2.6</td><td>2.9</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>2.3</td><td>2.6</td><td>2.9</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>2 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Henríquez-Hernández et al. 2023</td><td>2</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for beef, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>Henríquez-Hernández et al. 2023 is the only compatible sampling family for beef, as sold on this basis in the completed beef ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/henriquez-hernandez2023-baby-purees-spain-elements" class="internal" data-slug="sources/henriquez-hernandez2023-baby-purees-spain-elements" data-no-cite-meta>Henríquez-Hernández et al. 2023</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:beef-96813d0d59ae:b1fa8b8e55a2</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><div hidden data-form-reasons><p data-reason="no_numeric_value_or_bound" data-title="Spread or extreme value only">The source reports only a percentile, range or maximum for these samples, with no mean or median to place against the reference. Spread figures that do have a mean or median are shown on that row instead.</p><p data-reason="value_fails_source_integrity_check" data-title="Held">The value could not be reconciled with its own paper, so it is shown but not compared.</p><p data-reason="bounds_span_categories" data-title="Non-detect spans the bands">The result is below a reporting limit, and the range from zero to that limit crosses more than one band.</p><p data-reason="species_or_material_without_compatible_reference_after_full_ledger" data-title="No reference for this form">No medians or sample values exist for this form and metal, so no HMI reference could be built.</p><p data-reason="reference_below_display_minimum_after_full_ledger" data-title="Reference too small">The HMI reference for this form has fewer than four units or no measurable spread, below the display minimum.</p><p data-reason="basis_incompatible_with_all_references" data-title="Basis has no reference">The result is on a basis (dry weight, or not stated) that no HMI reference for this form uses, so it cannot be placed.</p><p data-reason="bounded" data-title="Limits overlap">Reporting limits overlap the study comparison, so no direction can be shown.</p></div><script type="application/octet-stream" data-explorer-payload data-encoding="base64"></script><div hidden data-explorer-details data-chunk-rows="100"><div hidden data-explorer-chunk="0"><script type="application/octet-stream" data-encoding="base64"></script><div data-evidence-content><p class="hmi-dataset-title"><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">WHO GEMS/Food</a></p><p>Beef, as sold · Lead (Pb) · 7 results.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Selected finding and reference</p><div class="hmi-selected-result" data-selected-finding><strong class="hmi-finding">36 µg/kg (median)</strong><span class="hmi-row-note">median.</span><p>7 results. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach beef

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach beef comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Beef, frozen from frozen beef, Sharkia retail sample 8F had total mercury higher at 450 µg/kg, against 80 µg/kg for all 15 frozen samples, Sharkia in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mohamed NH, Yahya G, El Bayoumi RM, Hussein MAM, Cavalu S, Dahshan H, Alsayeqh AF, Darwish WS, Nasr EAA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt">Detection and health risk assessment of toxic heavy metals in chilled and frozen meat collected from Sharkia province in Egypt</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Not reported</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, beef, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (2.05 µg/kg) and the highest in AFRO (36 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (0.55 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (10 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

In one study, lead across 20 groups of beef ranged from 11.1 µg/kg (Meradia Bazar (MB), Dhaka, phase 1) to 69.6 µg/kg (Malibug Bazar (MLM), Dhaka, phase 1); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/hossain2022-dhaka-market-beef-metals|19]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Hossain MM, Hannan ASMA, Kamal MM, Hossain MA · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/hossain2022-dhaka-market-beef-metals">Detection of heavy metals and evaluation of beef procured from the different market of Dhaka in Bangladesh</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">European Journal of Food Science and Technology 10(2):1-10</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/hossain2022-dhaka-market-beef-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 6 groups of beef ranged from 80 µg/kg (fresh meat, unit 3 (different manufacturer or supplier)) to 140 µg/kg (sausages, unit 3 (different manufacturer or supplier)); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/todorovska2023-north-macedonia-meat-fish-metals|20]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Todorovska N, Silovska Nikolova A, Pejkovski Z · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/todorovska2023-north-macedonia-meat-fish-metals">DETERMINATION OF As, Cd, Pb, Cu AND Zn IN MEAT, MEAT PRODUCTS AND FISH</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Agricultural, Food and Environmental Sciences 77(2) (2023) 86-91</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/todorovska2023-north-macedonia-meat-fish-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mohamed NH, Yahya G, El Bayoumi RM, Hussein MAM, Cavalu S, Dahshan H, Alsayeqh AF, Darwish WS, Nasr EAA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt">Detection and health risk assessment of toxic heavy metals in chilled and frozen meat collected from Sharkia province in Egypt</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Not reported</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, beef from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than beef from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mohamed NH, Yahya G, El Bayoumi RM, Hussein MAM, Cavalu S, Dahshan H, Alsayeqh AF, Darwish WS, Nasr EAA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt">Detection and health risk assessment of toxic heavy metals in chilled and frozen meat collected from Sharkia province in Egypt</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Not reported</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Beef, as sold from chilled beef, Sharkia retail sample 1C had lead higher at 720 µg/kg, against 640 µg/kg for all 15 chilled samples, Sharkia in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mohamed NH, Yahya G, El Bayoumi RM, Hussein MAM, Cavalu S, Dahshan H, Alsayeqh AF, Darwish WS, Nasr EAA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt">Detection and health risk assessment of toxic heavy metals in chilled and frozen meat collected from Sharkia province in Egypt</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Not reported</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mohamed2023-heavy-metals-beef-egypt">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-beef-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-beef-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of beef have the lowest levels?">

For total arsenic, the HMI reference median was lowest for beef, cooked (4.9 µg/kg) and highest for beef, canned (5.19 µg/kg); forms differ in water content, so this compares foods as sold or eaten, not uptake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Stojanović B, Janković S, Đorđević V, Marjanović S, Vasilev D, Stojanović Z, Balaban M, Antić V · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals">Determination of toxic elements in meat products from Serbia packaged in tinplate cans</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Research Square preprint, posted 26 February 2021 (version 1)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-beef" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-beef" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in beef?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in beef?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same beef.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants|21]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety (Hong Kong) · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Metallic Contaminants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Beef, cooked (all samples) had lead higher at 9 µg/kg, against 7 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (beef, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants|21]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety (Hong Kong) · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Metallic Contaminants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-beef-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-beef-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in beef is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in beef is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">
